items.q: What does Nate say Jev actually returns?
items.a: Three shapes: yes/no (he calls it a **null**), a **choice**, and a **score**, each with a confidence. It does not write, summarize, or find themes. Input cap on this tape: **64k** tokens. [[i-tested-jev-on-12-real-use-cases]]

Seven questions. Jev **~70 seconds and 9 cents**, then **6 seconds and 9 cents** after parallel payloads. Luna: **5 minutes and 62 cents**. He says 12× cost and 46× time. 46× matches the 6-second run.

items.q: Why can't he ask Jev what his meetings mean?
items.a: Open themes are a chat job. He pre-declares questions (owned next step, tension, waiting on Nate) and reads the counts. [[questions-are-the-analysis]]

items.q: What does he require before routing production to Jev?
items.a: A **golden set of 100** with known answers. Run Jev, Opus, and Soul. Keep the one that wins accuracy and cost, plus speed if the loop is live.
His Chrome extension. As an X post hits the screen, Jev tags it breaking, golden nugget, or AI slop. He says the first hour was weak.

items.q: Why does the paper trader fail the bill?
items.a: The model is about **$2/day** at one decision a second, 24/7. The exchange **fees cost more than Jev**. He calls the POC unvetted. Browser-use clips decide, then a second model has to type.
